verdict.rationale: cubic's automation config (review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions and custom agents) lives in a repo-root `cubic.yaml` that the docs call the source of truth. That puts it under git, so versioning, PR-based review and rollback are implied through normal source control. A community comment confirms this in-codebase approach. However, cubic documents no native version history, change review or rollback for its automations, and settings learned from feedback or the community agent library have no stated versioning at all. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of versioning/rollback for automations, change history or diff for custom agents and learned memory, a native rollback mechanism, hands-on corroboration.
